ARTICLE 7: PARKING
Section 7.1
GENERAL PROVISIONS
7.1.1 Intent
The primary purpose of this Article is to provide
adequate vehicular access to land uses in the city.
This Article, in combination with other provisions
of this Ordinance, is also intended to encourage
the use of public transportation, planned parking
structures, and flexible parking arrangements to
provide access to the Downtown and the Millyard
Districts, and to discourage the reliance on surface
parking lots to serve uses in these areas.
7.1.2 Applicability
A. Areas and Buildings Subject to
Parking Requirements
In any district, except the DT-2 District and the
Gaslight Historic Overlay District, if any structure
is constructed or enlarged or if any use of land is
established or changed, off-street parking spaces
provided by garage spaces or by open-air spaces
shall be provided for the entire use in accordance
with the parking requirements established by this
Article. Existing or new accessory parking or loading
spaces necessary to meet the requirements of this
Article in connection with any existing use shall
hereafter be maintained; except that they may be
relocated but not reduced in number.
B. Changes in Use or Expansion
of Existing Buildings
A change in or expansion of a use shall require
compliance with the number of parking, stacking,
and loading spaces required by this Article, except in
the case of a property that has received a Conditional
Use permit for reduced parking, which may continue
to provide reduced parking if the change in use does
not require more parking or loading spaces than the
use on which the permit was based.
C. Parking Exemptions and
Reductions
1. The DT-2 District and the Gaslight Historic
Overlay District are exempt from the on-site parking
minimums required in Table 7.2-A Off-Street Parking
Requirements .
2. The DT-1 and Millyard Districts shall provide on-
GENERAL PROVISIONS
site parking for one half (1/2) of what would otherwise
be required in Table 7.2-A Off-Street Parking
Requirements , except for Residential or Lodging
uses, which shall provide one parking space per
dwelling, rooming, or lodging unit.
3. Outdoor seating that is located on a sidewalk
within the public right-of-way and has been otherwise
approved by the City of Manchester is exempt from
parking minimums required in Table 7.2-A Off-Street
Parking Requirements. Outdoor seating on private
property is not exempt from parking minimums.
7.1.3 Use and Availability
Required parking spaces shall, at all times, be
available for the parking of vehicles of residents,
customers, patrons, or employees of the principal
use(s) that the spaces are intended to serve.
Required spaces shall not be used for storage of
vehicles, goods, or materials, or for the sale, repair,
or servicing of any vehicles, except for temporary
construction activities on the site.
7.1.4 Parking Access
Unless permitted as a tandem parking space by this
Article, all off-street parking shall have access to a
public right-of-way from the property on which it is
located. Such access may include travel across an
appurtenant easement that encumbers an adjoining
property and that has been recorded.
7.1.5 Plan Required
A plot plan drawn to scale, including the bounds
of the entire parcel and all structures and
impervious areas, is required for all building permit
applications and land use board applications for
new development, paving of driveways and parking
areas, or expansions of buildings. The plan shall
show the layout of all parking spaces, loading areas,
driveways, drive aisles, and required landscaping,
as applicable, for review for conformance with
this Ordinance by the Planning and Community
Development Department.
7.1.6 Conditional Use Permits for
Alternative Parking Arrangements
The Planning Board is authorized to issue Conditional
Use permits to reduce or alter the number of off-
street parking spaces otherwise required by this
Article. Such Conditional Use permits may be

A. Off-Premises Parking
Off-premises parking shall meet the requirements of
either (1) or (2) below, or a combination thereof:
1. Public Parking. The public parking available to the
proposed use, in combination with other uses placing
demands on such facilities, is sufficient in volume,
convenience, safety, and availability to satisfy the
anticipated parking demands of the proposed use.
2. Private Parking. Private parking spaces may be
provided off-site if the use served cannot practically
supply all of its parking on-site and the off-site parking
meets the following requirements:
a. The off-site parking spaces shall be dedicated
to the proposed use and reserved either with
pavement markings or signs;
b. The owner of the lot on which the off-site parking
is located shall be bound by a deed or long-term
lease, requiring the owner, its heirs, and its assigns
to maintain the required number of parking spaces
for the duration of the use served;
c. The off-site parking shall not be located within a
Residential (R) zoning district; and
d. Adequate provisions shall be made to assure
safe pedestrian access between the off-site parking
location and the proposed use.
3. Location of Parking. Whether off-premises
parking is public or private, it shall be within the
following number of feet, measured from the principal
entrance of the use served:
a. 500 feet from a residential use.
b. 1,000 feet from a non-residential use.
c. Parking may be located beyond these minimums
where a regular shuttle or similar means of
transportation is provided along a direct route from
the off-premises parking to the use.
B. Reduced Parking
The Planning Board may reduce the parking
minimums required in Table 7.2-A Off-Street Parking
Requirements upon a showing by the applicant that
the number of parking spaces required would not be
used and that such a reduction in parking would not
negatively impact surrounding properties.

STANDARDS
7.4.1 General Requirements
All driveways providing site access from a street,
alley, or other right-of-way shall be designed,
constructed, and maintained as required herein.
7.4.2 Driveway Dimensions
A. Driveway Width
The width of any entrance or exit driveway shall
not exceed 24 feet at its intersection with a lot line,
and shall be maintained for a minimum depth of 10
feet. Wider driveways not exceeding 36 feet in width
are permitted in the BC-2, IND, and Innovation (ID)
Districts.
B. Planning Board Modification
The Planning Board may allow an increase to the
maximum driveway width for an application over
which it has jurisdiction, upon finding that the
increased width:
1. Would not jeopardize pedestrian or motorist
safety; and
2. Would be consistent in character with surrounding
properties and the intent of the zoning district.
7.4.3 Driveway Locations
A. Distance of Driveways to
Intersecting Street
No portion of a driveway shall be closer than 20 feet
to the street lot line of an intersecting street.
B. Distance Between Driveways
within a Lot
The closest points of any two driveways leading from
the same street to a single lot shall not be within
30 feet of each other at their intersections with the
street lot line. On corner lots, the closest points of
driveways providing access to intersecting streets
shall be no closer than 50 feet as measured along
the property line and no closer than 36 feet as
measured diagonally between their closest points at
their intersection with the property line.

Section 9.1
GENERAL PROVISIONS
9.1.1 Purpose and Intent
The purpose of this Article is to regulate the display
of signs on privately owned property in a manner
that promotes the public interest in safety and
aesthetics, while maintaining neutrality as to the
content of speech. This Article is further intended to:
A. Communication and Navigation
Encourage the effective use of signs as a means of
communication and facilitate navigation from place
to place within the City;
B. Aesthetic Environment and
Economic Development
Maintain and enhance the aesthetic environment of
the City while retaining the City’s ability to attract and
encourage economic development;
C. Pedestrian and Traffic Safety
Improve pedestrian and traffic safety by eliminating
potential hazards;
D. Adverse Effects
Minimize possible adverse effects of signs on nearby
public and private property by eliminating excessive
and confusing sign displays;
E. Enforcement
Enable fair and consistent enforcement of these sign
regulations; and
F. Property Value
Safeguard property values by minimizing the possible
adverse effects of signs on nearby properties.
9.1.2 Permit Required
Except as otherwise provided in this Article, no sign
may be erected, placed, replaced, moved, enlarged,
illuminated, or substantially altered without a permit
in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance.
A. Filing of Permit and Fee
A permit application and fee shall be submitted to
the Director and shall include a set of plans at an
appropriate scale showing the location, size, method

Where freestanding signs are proposed, an accurate
plan of the lot, to scale, showing the location of
buildings, parking areas, driveways, and landscaped
areas shall be submitted.

Proposed Signs
An accurate representation, by photograph or plan,

illumination.
C. Proposed Sign Measurements
and Features
An accurate representation of the sign type, size,

illumination and attachment for all proposed signs.
9.1.4 Maintenance
All signs shall be maintained in good repair (e.g.,
without peeling paint or broken sign faces) and in
operable condition (e.g., if internally illuminated, all
light bulbs or tubes shall be operational) at all times.
The City may order the removal of any sign which
becomes a public hazard due to lack of maintenance
and repair.
9.1.5 Non-conforming Signs
A non-conforming sign that was lawfully established
and maintained in compliance with the provisions of
all applicable laws in effect at the time of original
installation, but that does not now comply with
the provisions of this Ordinance, may be repaired
subject to these additional regulations.
A. Compliance of Repairs
No non-conforming sign may be altered in any way
in structure or material, or re-located to a position,
that makes the sign less in compliance with the
requirements of this Ordinance than it was before
the alteration or relocation.
GENERAL PROVISIONS
B. Extent of Destruction
Should a nonconforming sign be destroyed by any
means to an extent of more than 75 percent of its
replacement cost at the time of its destruction, it
shall not be reconstructed except in conformity with
the provisions of this Ordinance.
9.1.6 Required Vegetation
Trees, shrubs, or other vegetation required by this
Ordinance shall not be destroyed or removed for
the purpose of installing, increasing, or enhancing
the visibility of any sign, unless replaced in-kind
elsewhere on the property.
9.1.7 Location
A. On the Principal Lot
A permanent sign, except for off-premises signs,
shall be located on the same site as the subject of
the sign.
B. Minimum Setbacks
The minimum setback for any freestanding sign shall
be five feet from any property line.
C. Signs on Public Property
No sign, other than signs placed by agencies of
government with appropriate jurisdiction, or a sign
whose placement is authorized by such agencies,
may be erected or placed on public property,
including rights-of-way.
D. Clear Sight Area
No sign may be installed in a way that obstructs free
and clear vision, clear sight area per Section 8.4,
Visibility at Intersections , or free use of any public
right-of-way, intersection, ingress or egress point,
transit stop, parking space, drive aisle, driveway,
building entrance, fire escape, or accessibility ramp.
E. Obstruction
No sign may obstruct or substantially interfere with
any window, door, fire escape, stairway, ladder, or
any other opening or structure intended to provide
ingress or egress to any building.

traffic control device.

through facility, only as permitted as an accessory

comply with the following standards.

per critical turning point (e.g., to direct vehicular traffic
to a drive-through window, loading area, etc);

surface area;

signs located within the clear sight area shall be limited
to three feet in height; and

situation, or event that is designed, intended, or
expected to take place or to be completed within
a reasonably short or definite period of time after
the erection of the sign; or a sign that is intended to
remain on the location where it is erected or placed
for a reasonably short or definite period of time after
the erection of the sign. If the sign display area is

sign.

PROHIBITED OR LIMITED

Ordinance is prohibited.

1. Signs which interfere with, obstruct the view of,

part of an electronic message center sign;

drivers and create a potential safety hazard;
5. Signs attached to a tree, street light, utility pole,
rock, or fence, except as permitted by Section 9.2.8
Construction Signs ; and
6. Signs on a building blocking windows.

Applications

(EMCs)
Any sign that uses computer-generated messages
or some other electronic means of changing copy.

lamps, LEDs, LCDs, or a flipper matrix. EMCs are
prohibited unless they comply with the following
regulations:
1. EMCs are permitted in all districts for Civic principal
uses, pursuant to Table 4.3-A, Principal Uses. Such

9.4.1 Surface Area
Unless otherwise stated, sign surface area is
calculated as the height of the sign multiplied by
the width of the sign. Sign surface area shall be
measured as follows:
A. Signs on a Background
The entire area of the framework or background of
the sign is calculated as sign area, including any
material or color forming the sign face or background
[IMAGE]
used to differentiate the sign from the structure
against which it is placed.
B. Signs with a Base
The base of a monument sign does not count as
sign area if it is less than three feet in height and is
constructed of masonry or a material that matches
the primary building façade material.
C. Individually Mounted Letters or
Features
The sign area is calculated as the total area of each
rectangle that encompasses each word or graphic
[IMAGE]
element. Sign area does not include any supporting
framework or bracing, unless such framework is part
of the message or sign face.
D. Signs on an Awning
The area of awning sign is calculated by drawing the
smallest possible rectangle that encompasses each
word or graphic element on the awning.
E. Two or More Faces
If the sign has two or more faces, the area of all
[IMAGE]
faces is included in determining the area of the sign.
However, if two sign faces are placed back to back,
or at an angle where both faces cannot be viewed
from any point at the same time, and are separated
by a maximum dimension of 42 inches measured
from the furthest points of each of the sign faces,
the sign surface area shall be computed by the
measurement of only one of the sign faces.

INTRODUCTORY PROVISIONS
Section 11.1
INTRODUCTORY
PROVISIONS
11.1.1 Authority and Purpose
The provisions of this Ordinance related to impact
fees are established pursuant to New Hampshire
RSA 674:21,V. The provisions of this Section
are intended to: assist in the implementation of
the City Master Plan; provide for the planning
for and provision of public capital facilities
necessitated by the growth of the City; and assess
an equitable share of the growth-related cost of
new and expanded public capital facilities to new
development, in proportion to the facility demands
created by that development. Facilities which are
eligible for inclusion under this Ordinance are
specifically enumerated under NH RSA 674:21,V
and are more specifically limited to those facilities
identified in the Impact Fee Schedule adopted by
the Board of Mayor and Aldermen.
11.1.2 Definitions
For the purposes of this Article, the following terms
shall be defined as such:
Feepayer: A person applying for the issuance
of a building permit which would create new
development.
New Development: An activity which results in:
1. The creation of one or more new dwelling
units; or
2. The conversion of a lawfully existing use, or
additions thereto, which would result in a net
change in the number of dwelling units; or
3. The construction of new non-residential
facilities, additions to existing non-residential
facilities, or conversion of property that results in
a net increase in the gross floor area of a non-
residential use; or
4. One or more subdivisions or site plans for the
purpose of assessing an impact fee.
Public Capital Facilities: Facilities and equipment
owned, maintained or operated by the City of
Manchester or the Manchester School District,
which are listed in the city of Manchester’s adopted
Impact Fee Schedule.
ARTICLE 11: IMPACT FEES
11.1.3 Findings
A. General
The City, through its Planning Board, has adopted
a City Master Plan and the Board of Mayor and
Aldermen has adopted a Capital Improvements
Program.
B. Purpose
The City is responsible for and committed to the
provision of public facilities and services, at standards
which support and protect the public health, safety
and welfare.
C. Method of Apportioning Capital
Costs to New Development
Calculation methodologies for impact fees, as
established in reports by the Planning Board,
represent fair, rational and proportional methods of
allocating capital facility costs to new development.
Based on the methodologies, impact fees will not
exceed the costs of:
1. Providing additional public capital facilities
necessitated by the new developments paying
impact fees; or
2. Compensating the City for expenditures made for
existing public facilities which were constructed in
anticipation of new growth and development.
11.1.4 Imposition of Public Capital
Facilities Impact Fee
Any person or firm who wishes to construct new
development within the City is hereby required to
pay a Public Capital Facilities Impact Fee in the
manner and amount set forth in Section 11.5 .

ADMINISTRATION OF FUNDS

Required

The City Finance Director shall record all fees paid,
by date of payment and the name of the person
making payment, and shall maintain an updated
record of the current ownership, tax map and lot
reference number of properties for which impact

period of at least six years.

At the end of each fiscal year, the City Finance
Director shall make a report to the Board of Mayor
and Aldermen, giving a particular account of all
Public Capital Facilities impact fee transactions
during the year.
11.3.5 Use of Funds
Funds withdrawn from the Public Capital Facilities
Impact Fee accounts shall be used solely for the
purpose of acquiring, constructing, expanding or
equipping those Public Capital Facilities identified in
the Impact Fee Schedule.

from the date of the final payment of such impact
fee, to appropriate the non-impact fee share of
related capital improvement costs.

Section 11.4
EXEMPTIONS AND WAIVERS
11.4.1 Exemptions
The following uses are exempt from selected impact
fees:
A. Age-Restricted Units
Those dwelling units within residential developments
in which occupancy will be legally and permanently
restricted to persons age 62 and over in accordance
with federal law are exempt from school impact fees.
B. Single Room Units
Single room dwelling units within a boarding, lodging,
or rooming house or within congregate housing that
have less than 350 square feet of gross floor area
are exempt from school impact fees.
C. Affordable Housing
New dwelling units that are legally restricted to
tenants whose income does not exceed 80 percent
of area median income and that are financed in
whole or in part with government-sponsored subsidy
shall be exempt from school impact fees. The legal
restriction shall be recorded at the Hillsborough
County Registry of Deeds and shall be in effect for a
minimum of 20 years.
11.4.2 Waivers
The Planning Board may grant a full or partial waiver
of an impact fee only in the following instances:
A. Credits for Other Public
Improvements
Land and/or Public Capital Facility improvements
may be offered by a fee payer as total or partial credit
toward the impact fee. The offer must be determined
to represent an identifiable dollar value computed
in a manner acceptable to the Planning Board and
shall meet the needs of the specific public facilities
for which the impact fees are adopted.
B. Documentation of No or
Substantially Reduced Demand
Where documentation and/or legally enforceable
mechanisms are provided to demonstrate to the
satisfaction of the Planning Board that a proposed
EXEMPTIONS AND WAIVERS
use will impose no or substantially reduced demands
on Public Capital Facilities, the Planning Board may
reduce or waive an impact fee. The documentation
and/or legally enforceable mechanisms shall be
submitted to the Planning Board in writing.
Improvements which would normally be required
by the Planning Board under the Subdivision or Site
Plan Review Regulations shall not be considered
eligible for waiver under this Article.
11.4.3 Application for Impact Fee
Waivers
The Planning Board may consider a request for
an impact fee waiver after a public hearing duly
noticed in conformance with the Subdivision and
Site Plan Review Regulations. The Planning Board
shall adopt an application fee to cover the costs of
administrative expenses and plan review consistent
with its application procedures. Applications for
impact fee waivers shall be made on the appropriate
application form available at the Planning and
Community Development Department and shall
include all materials required by the relevant
appendix. The applicant for an impact fee waiver
shall prepare and submit a written analysis of the
potential demand on Public Capital Facilities of the
new development activity. All costs incurred by the
City for the review of such study shall be paid by the
applicant.

1.3.1 PART 77 SURFACES DEFINED
To protect the safety of aircraft operations, the FAA defines 4 , 000

acceptable height of objects beneath them. Surface slopes
are express in terms of “run over rise ” where a 40:1 slope,
for example, represents a surface which rises one foot in
elevation for every forty feet of horizontal distance (40 foot
run for every 1 foot rise)
Primary Surface: The Primary Surface for all runways is
1000' wide with the edge parallel to runway centerline. The
primary surface extends 200 feet beyond the runway end
and is at the same elevation as the adjacent runway.
Approach Surfaces: The Precision Approach Surfaces for
Runways 06, 17, and 35 start 200 feet from the end of the
runway, have an initial width of 1,000 feet, and slope
upward at 50:1 for the first 10,000 feet and then slope at
40:1 for an additional 40,000 feet. The slope is based on
the distance along the extended centerline. The width of
the approach surface at 2,700 feet from the threshold is
1,750 feet. The Non-Precision Approach Surface for
Runway 24 starts 200 feet from the end of the runway, has
an initial width of 1,000 feet, and slopes upward at 34:1.
Horizontal Surfaces: The Horizontal Surfaces is defined by
10,000 foot arcs drawn from each runway end and
connected with tangents. The surface elevation is 150 feet
above the highest runway elevation.
Transitional Surface: The Transitional Surfaces extend
upward from the edges of the primary and approach
surfaces at a 7:1 slope, perpendicular to the runway
centerline. They end at the Horizontal Surface elevation.
Above the Horizontal Surface, the 7:1 transitional surfaces
for precision approaches extend outward and upward from
the 40,000 foot length of the 40:1 Approach Surface for a
distance of 5,000 feet. The slope is measured E
perpendicular to the runway centerline. L . 350

the Horizontal Surface and extends upward at a 20:1 slope
for a 4,000 foot distance. The slope is measured
perpendicular to the closest horizontal surface location. E L
